questions.q: What does the Performance Schema actually instrument, per this lesson?
options: Low-level server execution details like statement statistics, wait events, and memory usage
Only the physical disk space used by each database
User login history for security auditing only
The visual layout of query results
questions.explain: Performance Schema instruments internal code paths to expose statement execution stats, wait events, memory usage, and more.

questions.q: How does this lesson describe the architectural difference between Performance Schema and SQL Server's DMVs?
options: Performance Schema is configurable, ongoing instrumentation queried after the fact, unlike DMVs queried on-demand against current in-memory state
They are architecturally identical, just named differently
DMVs are a MySQL-only feature with no SQL Server equivalent
Performance Schema only works when the server is offline
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly frames Performance Schema as an ongoing, configurable instrumentation/collection system, distinct from DMVs' on-demand querying model.

questions.q: What is the relationship between the sys schema and Performance Schema, per this lesson?
options: sys schema is a set of human-readable views and functions built on top of Performance Schema data
sys schema replaces Performance Schema entirely in modern MySQL
sys schema and Performance Schema are unrelated, separate instrumentation systems
sys schema only works on MyISAM tables
questions.explain: sys schema presents the same underlying Performance Schema (and Information Schema) data in a friendlier, pre-aggregated way.

questions.q: Per this lesson, which schema would you check first for a quick, readable list of unused indexes?
options: sys schema, e.g. sys.schema_unused_indexes
Performance Schema's raw wait event tables
The mysql system schema
information_schema.TABLES exclusively
questions.explain: sys schema views like sys.schema_unused_indexes answer common questions directly and readably, which is its whole purpose.

questions.q: What does a 'digest' refer to in the context of Performance Schema, per this lesson?
options: A normalized representation of a SQL statement (literals stripped) used to group similar queries together
A compressed backup file format
A summary email sent to the DBA each morning
The final result row of an aggregate query
questions.explain: A digest normalizes similar statements (e.g., differing only in literal values) so they can be grouped and analyzed together in Performance Schema.
